summary: Admit bounded PEK batch label printing for one application through the existing label reader.

impacts.evidence: The existing tenant-scoped PEK account and capability path remain the source of the document request.
The bounded PDF is reduced to an opaque digest reference before leaving host transport.
The existing label endpoint is reused and the explicit format enum is additive.
No event envelope, event type or event payload changes.
The existing logistics.label.read capability and LabelRequest interface remain unchanged.
No database columns, mappings or durable provider payloads are added.
The numeric cargo code, response size, base64 data and PDF signature are bounded before artifact publication.
The existing label permission, active account and outbound policy continue to gate the read operation.
Existing logistics label lineage records the opaque artifact reference without PDF contents.
Repeated reads are deterministic for the same validated payload; ambiguous responses never fabricate a document.
The transport adds only a bounded fixed-host HTTPS POST under the existing host-mediated egress boundary.
Existing logistics timeout, rate and error normalization covers the additional PEK print request.
Removing the explicit format admission closes batch-print reads without migration.
Deterministic adapter and host tests verify type=multiple, cargo code, base64/PDF validation and opaque artifact prefix.
